title: Generative AI Designs De Novo Antibiotics (NG1 & DN1) Defeating Drug-Resistant Gonorrhea and MRSA in Mice
aiSystem: MIT Collins Lab Generative Fragment & Atom-Level Antibiotic AI
whyItMatters: Published in Cell, MIT researchers moved beyond screening existing libraries to generatively design 36M+ hypothetical molecules from scratch—yielding two novel antibiotics (NG1 and DN1) that cleared superbug infections in mice.
summary: Published in Cell on August 14, 2025, Aarti Krishnan, Melis Anahtar, Jacqueline Valeri, James J. Collins, and colleagues at MIT and the Broad Institute used two complementary generative deep-learning platforms (fragment-based genetic algorithms and unconstrained atom-by-atom variational/graph generative models) to design over 36 million completely novel chemical candidates targeting multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae and MRSA. After computational filtering for toxicity, synthetic accessibility, and structural novelty, the team synthesized 24 top designs and validated two structurally unprecedented leads—NG1 (targeting a novel bacterial membrane protein LptA in gonorrhea) and DN1 (disrupting MRSA membranes)—both of which cleared infections in mouse models.
technicalHighlights: Generated and screened >36 million previously nonexistent chemical structures from scratch rather than searching pre-built vendor libraries.
Lead candidate NG1 selectively killed multidrug-resistant Neisseria gonorrhoeae via a novel membrane-assembly target (LptA) and cured vaginal infection models in mice.
Second lead DN1 cleared topical MRSA skin infections in mice with a structurally distinct membrane-disrupting scaffold.
caveats: Validated in preclinical mouse infection models; extensive medicinal-chemistry optimization, pharmacokinetics, toxicology, and human clinical trials are still required before patient use.
institutions: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard

scoreRationale.foundational: Marks the inflection from AI screening existing chemical libraries (Halicin, Abaucin) to de novo generative design of structurally unprecedented, in-vivo-active antibiotics.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly addresses WHO priority drug-resistant pathogens (gonorrhea and MRSA) with novel mechanisms of action.
scoreRationale.verification: Peer-reviewed in Cell with chemical synthesis, mechanistic target elucidation, and in vivo mouse efficacy models.
scoreRationale.velocity: Explored 36 million hypothetical molecules computationally before synthesizing only 24 candidates in the wet lab.
